query: More than a century of research on conventional steels and other alloys has shown that exposure within certain temperature ranges can sharply reduce toughness and threaten safety in aerospace, shipping, and petrochemical applications. High-entropy alloys offer attractive strength, ductility, resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement, and wear resistance; however, their multicomponent chemistry complicates predictions of long-term mechanical reliability. Their resistance to rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation does not establish whether their toughness will remain stable after service-relevant heating, and this uncertainty limits engineering use. For a high-performance multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its as-designed condition, under the constraint that its original strength–ductility combination must be retained, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to reduce post-exposure toughness degradation? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to an otherwise identical untreated baseline, define the temperature, duration, and loading boundaries, identify supporting evidence from the observations summarized above, and describe a decisive experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Grain refinement via severe plastic deformation can reduce post-exposure toughness degradation in high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: As-designed high-entropy alloy with original strength-ductility combination
generation.intervention: Severe plastic deformation to refine grain structure
generation.mechanism: Reduced grain size leads to increased grain boundary area, which can impede dislocation movement and reduce toughness degradation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved toughness retention after service-relevant heating
generation.baseline: Untreated high-entropy alloy with original grain structure
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 473-1223 K, Duration: up to 3 days, Loading: uniaxial tensile tests
generation.uncertainty: Effect of severe plastic deformation on high-entropy alloy microstructure and properties is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Compare toughness of severely plastically deformed high-entropy alloy with untreated baseline after service-relevant heating
measurements: Toughness measurements via Charpy impact test or fracture toughness testing
Microstructural analysis via TEM or SEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If severely plastically deformed high-entropy alloy shows no significant improvement in toughness retention compared to untreated baseline, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: What alloying and scaling conditions lead to the strongest both ductile and stable materials?. System: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (HEA) thin films and pillars. Processing: d.c. magnetron co-sputtering on (100) silicon or sapphire substrates at room temperature; Ion beam-assisted deposition (IBAD) used with 1.2 keV beam energy, 5 mA current, and 35° incidence angle to reduce grain size; Focused Ga ion beams (FIB) used to mill pillars with diameters of ~1 μm, 500, 200, and 100 nm. Test conditions: Microcompression tests at a strain rate of 2 × 10−3 s−1; Thermal annealing at 1,100 °C for 3 days in argon atmosphere.
